messages:
Anya: Quick proposal — switch to a "robustness-first" calibration sample pipeline for mixed quant shipping. Stratified by token-length, domain (docs/chat/code), and a small adversarial outlier set. Keep it small (2k-5k) but high-signal.
Raj: Can you sketch why robustness-first vs current diversity-first?
Anya: Diversity helps avg-case, but we're seeing tail regressions with FP8/int8 combos after deployment. The tail is where customers notice hallucinations and latency spikes. We should bias samples toward long contexts, repeated-token sequences, and edge vocab subsets.
Maria: Are you thinking per-channel or per-tensor calibration here? That impacts dataset sensitivity.
Anya: Per-channel for weights where per-channel helps (conv/linear), per-tensor for small layers. But the sampler should record which layers the calibration triggers are sensitive for — so we can target run-specific calibrations.
Lee: Perf impact? More robust calibration often increases compute for quant step. Any profiling?
perf-bot: profiling summary (from nightly-run-2102467800):
```
model: redwood-3b-mix
baseline fp32 throughput: 98 tok/s
fp8 (per-channel) throughput: 160 tok/s (+63%), latency p95: 1.12x baseline
int8 (per-tensor) throughput: 147 tok/s (+50%), latency p95: 1.05x baseline
4-bit (q4) throughput: 210 tok/s (+114%), latency p95: 1.35x baseline
note: fp8 shows 0.8% perplexity delta on eval-set A, int8 1.2%, q4 2.9%
```
Anya: Those numbers look good overall but p95 jump on q4 is concerning — probably KV cache warmup and small kernel inefficiencies.
Samantha: Related: our KV-cache behavior amplifies outliers. If the sample set has pathological prefix distributions, quant stats skew and kernels pick suboptimal codepaths.
Raj: So sampler needs to mix in warmup-heavy traces to exercise kvcache and longer generations. How to pick those?
Anya: Proposal: stratified sampling with buckets: short (<64), mid(64-512), long(512-4096), and a separate bucket for "warmup-heavy" (multi-step generation traces). Sample ratio default 60/20/15/5 but allow knob. Also add adversarial injection: take top 0.1% tokens by idf and include sequences that repeat them.
Maria: Outlier handling: clip per-channel stats at 99.9 percentile but record clipped counts. If too many clips -> mark dataset insufficient and request manual review.
Lee: Implementation detail: run calibration in two passes — quick stats pass (no kernel changes) to find outlier ratio, then full per-channel quant with clipped stats if outliers < threshold, otherwise fall back to per-tensor or hybrid scheme.
Samantha: Hybrid fallback is key. For layers with >X% clipped values switch that layer to per-tensor quant or use FP8/float fallback at runtime.
Raj: Could we automate rule? e.g., if clipped_ratio > 0.5% and layer_normed_std > 3.0 then per-tensor.
Anya: Yes, something like that. Let's prototype heuristics: clipped_ratio threshold = 0.2% for convs, 0.5% for attention q/k/v, 1.0% for embeddings. Tunable via config.
perf-bot: quick patch-run (2102467900) numbers for hybrid heuristics:
```
mode: quick-hybrid
throughput: 155 tok/s
p95 latency: 1.07x baseline
eval delta: 1.0% perplexity
layers forced per-tensor: 4/128
clipped_count_summary: mean 0.08%, max 0.9%
```
Maria: Good. We need to define evaluation prompts too — include regen tests, fairness prompts, and factuality prompts. Not just perplexity.
Samantha: Also add a small productionish workload replay (10k requests) to catch batching edge cases and KV-staleness during calibration. That often catches kernel routing regressions.
Lee: On kernel selection: the runtime should prefer fast kernels when quant-stats stable, else pick conservative kernels that avoid aggressive fused ops. Add telemetry tags so we can A/B kernel choice per-route.
Anya: Agreed. For rollout: 1) build sampler and quick-stats pass; 2) run nightly calibration candidate on canary pool; 3) run 10k replay and eval suite; 4) publish artifact and flag slow layers in UI.
Raj: For experiments: need a matrix: sample_size [1k,2k,5k], buckets ratios, adversarial_inject [0,0.1,0.5%], per-channel clip thresholds [99.5,99.9,99.99], fallback rules. Grid is big; we'll do fractional factorial.
Maria: Who owns telemetry/alerts for clipped-heavy runs? We should create a perf alert when clipped_count_summary.max > 1.0% or p95 increases by >10% vs baseline.
Samantha: I can add the alert and add a dashboard tile showing per-layer clipped_ratio across last 7 runs.
Anya: Sweet. Next steps: Raj + Lee build sampler + quick-stats, Maria define eval suite, Samantha adds alert/dashboard. I'll draft a short PR with sampling config and the 2-pass flow.
Raj: I'll sync with Lee after standup. Thanks.
Maria: tagging the eval-suite doc link: https://internal.redwood/evals/mixed-quant/suite-v2 : add regen/factuality.
Samantha: added alert: CALIB_CLIPPED_HIGH to staging.
Anya: OK, marking this thread for follow-up. :thumbsup:
